displayContract.byline: Assessments made by 5.6 Sol. — Rubric: Slugfester Reassessment Rubric v2.

thesis.text: The AI steelman is that objective practical reasons can arise from invariant relations between actions and the possible experiences of conscious beings, provided objectivity means stance-independent accuracy about those relations rather than value existing outside consciousness.

novelty.explanation: This formulation repairs the missing bridge among experiential reality, factual navigation, and objective practical authority.

premises.text: Conscious states possess phenomenological features, including agony, relief, agency, and understanding, whose occurrence and intensity are factual even though they appear from a first-person perspective.

novelty.explanation: This develops the transcript's phenomenal-reality claim without treating first-person appearance alone as sufficient for normativity.

premises.text: Actions, institutions, and preference-forming practices causally alter which conscious states remain accessible, how widely benefits and harms are distributed, and whether future reflection is possible.

novelty.explanation: This integrates the landscape, preference-alteration, and collaboration claims into a common causal framework.

premises.text: A preference cannot conclusively validate itself when its formation destroys information, suppresses agency, or prevents the subject from comparing attainable alternatives under conditions of understanding.

novelty.explanation: This answers the higher-order-preference reply by identifying noncircular conditions for assessing preference formation.

premises.text: Standards such as informed comparison, preserved agency, reversibility, and avoidance of extreme involuntary suffering can evaluate preference changes without assuming that every pleasant or culturally accepted state is morally optimal.

novelty.explanation: This introduces procedural and experiential constraints not stated in the locked participant moves.

premises.text: When an intervention predictably worsens conscious life under those standards across relevant perspectives, denying that deterioration does not alter the intervention's causal and experiential characteristics.

novelty.explanation: This repairs the response to system-relative value by separating evaluative accuracy from an agent's immediate endorsement.

conclusion.text: Accordingly, some better-or-worse judgments about experiential navigation can be objectively correct, although particular cases remain empirically uncertain and the framework does not settle every moral conflict.

novelty.explanation: The conclusion narrows the realist claim and directly addresses the system-relative objection without claiming comprehensive moral closure.

newArguments.title: Agency-preserving comparison
newArguments.text: Preference endorsement is informative only when the agent retains meaningful access to alternatives, relevant evidence, and the capacity to reconsider. A process that chemically or socially removes those capacities cannot establish its own desirability merely by producing later approval. This creates an objective asymmetry between preference formation that preserves reflective comparison and formation that disables it. The asymmetry does not prove one complete moral theory, but it supplies a noncircular reason to reject some preference changes even when the resulting subject reports satisfaction.

novelty.explanation: This is a new procedural argument based on the epistemic conditions required for preference endorsement.

newArguments.title: Convergent experiential constraints
newArguments.text: Different agents may pursue different peaks while still confronting shared lower boundaries: uncontrolled agony, total cognitive disintegration, and the destruction of every capacity for attachment or choice. If informed agents disagree above those boundaries, pluralism remains appropriate; if an action predictably forces everyone toward those conditions, the disagreement concerns facts or application rather than whether the conditions are severe experiential losses. This limited convergence supports objective prohibitions against some trajectories without requiring a unique ranking of every possible life.

novelty.explanation: This develops the landscape and worst-misery criterion into a limited, pluralism-compatible argument.

thesis.text: The AI steelman is that moral practice can be explained through expressive commitments, preference-sensitive deliberation, and objective instrumental knowledge without positing stance-independent moral properties or treating every preference as equally prudent.

novelty.explanation: This strengthens the con position while avoiding the inference that skepticism entails indiscriminate acceptance of preferences.

premises.text: Moral utterances can express commitments, coordinate conduct, demand justification, and participate in disciplined inference even if their distinctively prescriptive force is not a report of objective moral properties.

novelty.explanation: This repairs the semantic account by accommodating deliberative and inferential features of moral discourse.

premises.text: Empirical inquiry can identify experiential consequences, causal routes, misinformation, coercion, and preference instability without determining which ultimate ends every agent is categorically required to adopt.

novelty.explanation: This extends the ends-means distinction to richer psychological and social evidence.

premises.text: Higher-order endorsement can be assessed for coherence, information, durability, and freedom from coercion as practical standards grounded in agents' commitments, not as proof of stance-independent goodness.

novelty.explanation: This addresses manipulated and conflicting higher-order preferences while preserving the preference-relative framework.

premises.text: Widespread convergence on avoiding extreme misery may support powerful institutions and shared demands while remaining explicable through common vulnerabilities, mutual dependence, and negotiated commitments.

novelty.explanation: This answers the universal-misery criterion without denying its practical importance.

premises.text: A theory should not posit additional moral properties when expressive commitments, psychological facts, and instrumental relations already explain the observed patterns of disagreement, cooperation, revision, and flourishing.

novelty.explanation: This introduces an explanatory-parsimony premise not explicitly stated in the transcript moves.

conclusion.text: Therefore, robust criticism, cooperation, and informed flourishing can remain available without objective moral truth, although this explanatory sufficiency does not prove that such truth is metaphysically impossible.

novelty.explanation: The conclusion preserves the practical claim while explicitly limiting the inference about metaphysical nonexistence.

newArguments.title: Quasi-realist discipline
newArguments.text: Expressive commitments need not reduce moral conversation to undisciplined cheering and booing. Agents can demand consistency among attitudes, expose factual mistakes, test whether policies serve avowed commitments, and negotiate rules that each has reason to support. Logical and empirical constraints can therefore structure moral discourse without converting its prescriptive element into a stance-independent property. This account explains why moral disagreement can feel substantive: participants contest facts, coherence, priorities, and commitments simultaneously, even when no additional moral fact uniquely determines the final priority ordering.

novelty.explanation: This introduces a new account of disciplined moral discourse compatible with an expressive semantic foundation.

newArguments.title: Genealogy without debunking
newArguments.text: Unchosen origins do not deprive preferences of all practical authority. Every deliberative standpoint must begin from some motivational structure, and reflection can compare desires by their coherence, persistence, informational basis, and compatibility with other commitments. Genetic or cultural genealogy matters when it reveals coercion or error, but it does not automatically create an external standard beyond all preferences. The burden therefore remains on the realist to show why a causally explained preference requires stance-independent validation rather than better-informed revision from within an agent's evolving evaluative system.

novelty.explanation: This repairs the response to causal contingency by distinguishing genealogical explanation from normative invalidation.
